I am a 46-year-old woman farming in Iringa, and this small beans plot of 0.06 hectares is part of my family's land. I will not buy chemical fertilizer because it is too expensive and beans are legumes that can fix nitrogen from the air, but I will spread manure from our animals to keep the soil fertile. I have saved bean seeds from last season's harvest, so I will plant those local seeds rather than buying new ones from the shop. My family and I will do all the work ourselves — planting, weeding, and harvesting — because the plot is small enough to manage without hiring anyone, and we rely on the rains so there is no need to irrigate.
